speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe your diarrhea in terms of frequency, duration, and whether it contains blood or mucus? Also, have you experienced any unintentional weight loss or fever recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if you drank untreated water or ate undercooked food while camping, and have you noticed any joint pain or skin rashes? I will also request a stool ova and parasite exam and a CBC to check for inflammation. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Ova_and_Parasites REQUEST TEST: CBC

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the stool test was normal, I want to rule out inflammatory bowel disease. Have you had any rectal bleeding, and does your diarrhea typically occur at night or wake you from sleep? REQUEST TEST: Stool_Calprotectin

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal inflammatory markers and the history of camping, I suspect Giardia lamblia despite the initial negative stool test, so I will request a specific Giardia antigen test and a colonoscopy to rule out microscopic colitis. REQUEST TEST: Giardia_Antigen REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative workup for infection and inflammation, I suspect Irritable Bowel Syndrome. Do you find that your symptoms worsen during times of stress, and have you noticed any changes in stool consistency related to your menstrual cycle?

speaker: Doctor
text: The mention of the ill camping companion suggests a lingering infectious etiology, so I will request a PCR panel for gastrointestinal pathogens to detect low-level infections missed by standard tests. REQUEST TEST: GI_PCR_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the extensive negative workup for infection, inflammation, and structural disease, I will request an abdominal CT scan to rule out other organic causes before finalizing my diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: With all organic and infectious causes ruled out, I am confident in diagnosing Irritable Bowel Syndrome based on your chronic symptoms and normal test results. DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
